questions.prompt: orders has 1,000,000 rows in 200 partitions. countries has 250 rows. Roughly how many rows does a broadcast join move over the network?
questions.explanation: Only the small side moves: one copy of its 250 rows to each of the 200 partitions of the big side. A shuffle join would move all 1,000,250 rows.

questions.prompt: Left table keys: [1, NULL]. Right table keys: [NULL, 1]. How many rows does an INNER join on key return?
questions.explanation: Only key 1 matches. In SQL, NULL = NULL is not true, so NULL keys never join.

questions.prompt: For `big LEFT JOIN small`, why can't the planner broadcast `big` even if it's under the threshold?
options: Broadcasting is only allowed for inner joins
A left row's unmatched status is only known by a task that sees all candidate right rows, so the preserved left side has to be streamed past a full copy of the right side
Spark doesn't support broadcasting the left side of any join
questions.explanation: If the left side were split across tasks that each saw only part of the right side, each task could wrongly emit (row, NULL). The build side must be the non-preserved side.

questions.prompt: Why is sort-merge Spark SQL's default for joining two large tables?
options: Sorting can spill to disk, so it works even when neither side's partitions fit in a hash table
questions.explanation: Hash joins need the build side of each partition in memory. Sort-merge streams two sorted runs, which scales to inputs bigger than memory.
